updates.text:
- When a task requires a hot object and you are at a microwave while holding the target object, use the direct `heat <object> with microwave 1` action before moving the object into the microwave.
- Do not move the target into the microwave and then close it expecting to heat it later; observed failures left the object unheated and ended at the step limit.
- Preserve successful direct heating while holding the target at the microwave, as when P2 heats plate 3 and P3 heats potato 3 before container interaction.

- When a task requires multiple target instances and a known location contains one or more still-needed visible instances of the target, and you are not already carrying a needed target instance, go there and take one needed instance (or as many as you can carry) up to the remaining required count before searching unsearched locations.
- After placing a retrieved instance in the chosen target receptacle, if that same known location still visibly contains another needed instance and the task is still unmet, return there before searching unsearched locations.
- Do not take extra instances beyond the remaining required count.

- When a task requires placing multiple target instances in a receptacle, after the first target instance is placed in a receptacle, use that same receptacle for subsequent target instances and keep the already-placed instance there.
- Do not move an already-placed target instance to a different receptacle as an experiment or while searching; only move it if the current receptacle is invalid or the task completion requires a different configuration.
- If the target receptacle is unspecified (e.g., “in drawer”), any suitable receptacle may be chosen, but once chosen, consolidate all required target instances there.

- While a multi-instance task is unmet, prioritize a previously visited location that was seen to contain a still-needed target instance as a source; after placing a retrieved instance, return there if it still contains another needed instance before searching other unsearched locations.
- If no such known source remains, check unsearched candidate surfaces and containers before revisiting locations already observed to be empty or already checked without finding the target. Do not repeatedly toggle or open/close the same container or shuttle the same object between locations.
- Expand search across all candidate types, including remaining drawers, shelves, cabinets, sidetables, countertops, diningtables, tvstands, coffeetables, sofas, and armchairs, rather than cycling through the same subset.
